english: Two groups of observations have the same coefficient of variation $20\%$. The first group has $30$ observations with mean $40$, and the second group has $20$ observations with mean $60$. Then the coefficient of variation, in per cent, of all $50$ observations taken together is
hindi: प्रेक्षणों के दो समूहों का विचरण गुणांक समान, $20\%$, है। पहले समूह में $30$ प्रेक्षण हैं जिनका माध्य $40$ है, तथा दूसरे समूह में $20$ प्रेक्षण हैं जिनका माध्य $60$ है। तब सभी $50$ प्रेक्षणों को साथ लेने पर विचरण गुणांक (प्रतिशत में) है
solution: CV $=\dfrac{8\sqrt3}{48}\cdot100=\dfrac{50}{\sqrt3}$ ($\approx28.9$; dropping the between-group term would give (A))
solution_full: So pooling two equally consistent groups with different means gives a less consistent whole; the within-group part alone gives $\sqrt{96}/48\times100=\dfrac{25\sqrt6}{3}$, and averaging the CVs gives $20$, both wrong.
originality_note: New: two groups equally consistent by CV are pooled, and the pooled CV rises because of the between-group variance; the numbers make the within and between parts equal (96 + 96) (way 4: hidden structure making the computation clean). Closest known: 'which of two groups is more consistent'. Different because: the CVs are equal and the question is about the pooled group, so the combined-variance formula is essential.
stem_review: Read as a student: every observation, class, symbol and condition is introduced before use, each sentence has one reading; the answer was recomputed independently in Python (exact fractions / sympy), is unique and equals the Answer Plan. Changed: No change.
key_step: Recovering the SDs from the CVs and including the between-group term in the pooled variance.
justification: Three formulae chained with a conceptual trap (CV does not average, the between-group term matters) and options built on the traps. Above the routine 2026-P2-Q12 (L2); a two-idea link at Level 3.

concept_use.Variance of a combination of two series: The pooled variance 96 + 96 = 192 including the between-group term.
concept_use.Coefficient of variation and comparison: The group SDs come from CV = 20, and the answer is the pooled CV 50/sqrt3.
